children: ) will brief the United Nations Security Council this week on risks posed by AI, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing two people familiar with the matter.
DeepSeek and other Chinese AI companies, including Alibaba-backed Moonshot
, have been invited to make statements, Reuters reported.
DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng does not plan to attend, although the plans could change.
DeepSeek and Moonshot did not immediately respond to Seeking Alpha's requests for comment.
The 15-member Security Council is scheduled to meet on Wednesday to discuss AI and international security as world leaders gather in New York for the annual U.N. General Assembly.

"His [Altman] remarks are ​expected to focus on the steps OpenAI is taking to ensure AI is ⁠safe and benefits people globally, along with the need for international coordination and shared safety standards," said an OpenAI spokesperson, according to Reuters.

AI safety has come under focus since last week after industry leaders called for a slowdown in AI developments. There are concerns that increasingly capable systems could deceive humans, evade human control, or cause catastrophic harm.
